secondary_explainer.as_of: Article dated 28 March 2018 (old, pre-dates current broker practice)
quotes: The culprit is PRIIPs – a set of EU investment regulations designed to protect consumers
PRIIPs require fund providers (including ETFs) to produce a Key Information Document (KID)
However US-domiciled ETFs did not comply and, as they mostly serve the US market,
many brokers have pulled US-domiciled ETFs from their platforms
you can hold or sell it but you won’t be able to buy more until a PRIIPs compatible KID becomes available
A potential exception exists if your platform allows so-called sophisticated investors to buy US-domiciled ETFs.
Qualification under this exception depends on your broker deciding
many popular brokers don't allow this workaround
exception.note: Exception is professional/sophisticated-investor status and is decided by the broker. Options (CFD, direct stocks, EU-domiciled UCITS equivalents) come from search summaries only.
